text:
alex: heads up — I ran into a weird ESM/CJS breakage that only shows up when a package uses conditional exports + dynamic import in edge builds. reproducible across webpack, rollup, and vite.

chen: ugh that sounds messy. can you paste the minimal repro? :eyes: 

alex: short repro: package uses conditional exports like: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "node": "./dist/node-entry.js"
  }
}
```
and the app does `await import('my-lib')` from an edge worker bundler output.

sam: what error do you see when running the edge bundle?

alex: with vite dev build on edge runtime I get: 
```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot set property 'exports' of #<Object>
    at __toCommonJS (chunk-helpers.js:12)
    at eval (index.js:5)
```
with webpack production build I get `Module not found: Can't resolve './dist/esm/index.js'` even though it exists in the package.

maria: lol conditional exports + dynamic import = spec corner. Could be resolver choosing the wrong entry because bundler does static analysis. Does the package publish both cjs+esm with correct package.json fields?

alex: yes, publishing has both. node resolution is fine on node16 via `import()` but in our edge target the bundler rewrites dynamic imports at build time and loses the conditional mapping. repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/edge-conditional-imports (small) — `npm i && npm run build:vite` reproduces.

chen: can you drop the actual minimal source snippet? e.g. app index using dynamic import + the import target path?

alex: sure — app/src/worker.js: `export default async () => { const lib = await import('my-lib'); return lib.createClient(); }`
and my-lib has `package.json` exports above and `dist/esm/index.js` has `export function createClient() { return 'ok' }`.

dev-bot: deploy-check: noticed edge-target bundler replaces dynamic import with a wrapper that expects a cjs default export. Might be mis-detecting because `package.json` has both `module` and `main`.

sam: I think the root cause: when bundlers pre-resolve dynamic imports they run their own package resolution logic and some use `exports` incorrectly for conditional 'node' vs 'import' qualifiers. Vite's resolver (esbuild-based) sometimes prefers `module` over `exports` when `exports` is conditional. Webpack has its own resolver plugin chain.

maria: repro idea: try adding an explicit `./index` entry that points to the ESM build (a non-conditional path) and see if that makes bundlers pick the ESM version. Also try `import('my-lib/dist/esm/index.js')` as a workaround.

alex: tried the explicit path workaround — it fixes vite and rollup but webpack still bundles the CJS variant into the worker and fails at runtime.

chen: can we get a failing webpack config? I'll spin one up and test `resolve.mainFields` ordering; webpack defaults to ['browser','module','main'] for browser builds — edge target might need `mainFields: ['module','main']` to prefer ESM.

sam: also check `package.json` top-level `type` field. If package has "type": "module" but still ships CJS files, some bundlers get confused on dynamic import emitted helper wrappers.

alex: repro includes `type: "module"`. removing that makes webpack happier but breaks serverside node consumers that rely on exact ESM semantics. Not acceptable as final fix.

maria: plan: 1) add a minimal failing webpack + vite + rollup config in the repro, 2) capture bundle output snippet where the import resolution is rewritten, 3) try to produce a small patch for our edge rollup plugin to respect `exports` conditional fields.

chen: i'll own the webpack test. assign to me. sam can you take rollup? maria take vite. alex can you add the three configs and logs to the repro? add exact commands.

alex: done — pushed configs and logs to the repro under /tests/ with `npm run build:webpack|vite|rollup` and bundle outputs. see link above. also pasted the failing stack traces in `tests/notes.md`.

dev-bot: FYI pinned to triage board #devex-bundler at priority P2.

sam: early quick workaround we used in product: publish a tiny `exports` fallback mapping that includes a `browser` key pointing explicitly to the esm build: "browser": "./dist/esm/index.js" That makes browser-targeted bundlers pick ESM. Might be a safe short-term fix.

alex: added `browser` mapping as a temporary patch in the repro — it fixes vite + rollup + webpack when testing locally. leaving as a patch but we need a broader doc/docs fix: guidance for package maintainers + our SDK publishing scripts to ensure correct mappings.

maria: also noticed typings break: TS `types` points to `dist/types/index.d.ts` but conditional exports don't surface type entry so editors can't resolve path when consumers import via bare `my-lib`. We should add `types` + `typesVersions` or publish a `types` entry under `exports` map.

chen: next steps: write a devex doc called "Packaging for edge: conditional exports, dynamic import, and bundler pitfalls". include recommended package.json minimal shape, and short-term SDK publish script change to include a `browser` export and explicit `exports['./package.json']` entry mapping for types.

sam: noted. i'll prepare rollup plugin checklist for maintainers.

alex: thanks all. leaving the repro link and marking the thread resolved once docs PR is open. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — ping me when the PR is up, i'll review for typings section.

chen: i'll post my webpack findings in the repo by EOD.

alex: cool — closing here for now.
